issues.legal_issue: Requiring a landlord to let a vacant dwelling to a privately selected tenant is not an unreasonable restriction on the landlord’s property right when the dwelling is not needed for the landlord’s own use and the selection serves the public need for housing.
material_facts: The owner notified the Controller that the house had become vacant after making an arrangement for alterations and a proposed letting to one applicant.
Two people applied to rent the house, and the Controller selected one of them rather than the applicant preferred by the owner.
The rent fixed was the rent demanded by the owner.
The owner’s challenge to the selection was rejected on appeal and in revision.
The statutory scheme allowed the owner to make representations about the proposed tenant’s suitability and provided for review of the selection.
issues.conclusion: The provision permitting selection of a private individual as tenant was valid and did not impose an unreasonable restriction on the owner’s property right.
issues.legal_principle: Article 19(1)(f), subject to Article 19(5), permits reasonable restrictions in the interests of the general public. The Act’s preamble identified housing regulation, rent control, and prevention of unreasonable eviction as its purposes. A vacant house not needed by its owner could be made available to a person in need of accommodation; a private individual is a member of the public. The suitability requirement, the owner’s opportunity to make representations, and review under sections 15 and 17 safeguarded against an unsuitable selection. No earlier case was relied on for this issue.

rule.if: constitutional_challenge_to_compulsory_tenant_selection and vacant_dwelling_not_needed_by_owner and selection_serves_housing_need and tenant_suitability_is_considered and owner_representation_and_review_are_available

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_compulsory_t: A property owner challenges a legal scheme that requires letting a vacant dwelling to a tenant selected by an authority.
predicates.vacant_dwelling_not_needed_by_owner: The dwelling is vacant and the owner does not need it for the owner’s own use.
predicates.selection_serves_housing_need: The authority’s selection makes accommodation available to a person in need of housing.
predicates.tenant_suitability_is_considered: The authority considers whether the proposed tenant is suitable before selecting that tenant.
predicates.owner_representation_and_review_are_avai: The owner can present views about the proposed tenant and seek review of the selection.

issues.definition: When an owner challenges compulsory tenant selection, the restriction is reasonable if the dwelling is not needed by the owner, selection serves housing need, and suitability and the owner’s opportunity to object and seek review are considered.

issues.legal_issue: A statutory power to select a tenant does not violate equality merely because it leaves the authority to choose among applicants where the selection is guided by suitability, applicants have an equal opportunity, and the owner’s views and review are provided for.
material_facts: The owner challenged the tenant-selection power under the equality guarantee after the Controller selected one applicant over another.
The owner’s views about the proposed tenant were to be considered, and the statutory scheme required the selected tenant to be suitable.
The scheme allowed people to apply for selection and provided an appeal to a District Judge and revision to the High Court.
The owner’s challenge to the selection was rejected by both the appellate and revisional courts.
issues.conclusion: The equality challenge failed: the owner could not rely on the provision to claim discrimination between owners, and, in any event, the selection scheme supplied adequate guidance and safeguards against arbitrary choice.
issues.legal_principle: Article 14 prohibits arbitrary discrimination. The Court held that this owner could not challenge the provision on the ground that it enabled discrimination between owners. It also held that, even if a tenant raised the challenge, the suitability requirement, equal opportunity to apply, consideration of the owner’s views, and judicial review supplied adequate guidance. Section 3(3)(a), its explanation identifying certain persons as unsuitable, and the review provisions in sections 15 and 17 informed that conclusion. No earlier case was relied on for this issue.

rule.if: constitutional_challenge_to_tenant_selection and ((challenger_is_owner and selection_power_does_not_discriminate_between_owners) or (applicants_have_equal_opportunity and suitability_guides_selection and owner_views_are_considered and judicial_review_is_available))

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_tenant_selec: A person challenges a legal scheme that authorizes an authority to select a tenant for a vacant dwelling.
predicates.challenger_is_owner: The person bringing the equality challenge owns the dwelling affected by the selection.
predicates.selection_power_does_not_discriminate_be: The selection power does not classify or treat one owner differently from another.
predicates.applicants_have_equal_opportunity: People seeking the dwelling are allowed an equal opportunity to apply for selection.
predicates.suitability_guides_selection: The authority must choose a tenant considered suitable and compare applicants’ claims.
predicates.owner_views_are_considered: The authority must consider the owner’s views about the proposed tenant.
predicates.judicial_review_is_available: The selection can be challenged through judicial appeal or revision.

issues.definition: An equality challenge to tenant selection fails if the owner’s challenge concerns a power that does not discriminate between owners, or if applicants have equal opportunity and selection is guided by suitability with the owner’s views and judicial review available.
